past_medical_history: No prior neuromuscular or autoimmune disease

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented x4. Normal language and cognition.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Bilateral ptosis, left greater than right — levator excursion left 5mm, right 8mm. Fatigable ptosis on sustained upgaze complete in left eye at 40 seconds. Horizontal diplopia on rightward gaze. Mild limitation of right eye adduction. Pupils equal, 3mm, reactive. No proptosis. Bilateral mild facial weakness.
neurological_exam.motor: Proximal upper extremity weakness: deltoids 4/5 bilaterally, worse on left. Proximal lower extremity: hip flexors 4+/5. Distal strength 5/5. Neck flexors 4/5. Classic fatigability: deltoid strength drops from 4 to 3/5 after 10 repetitions.
neurological_exam.gait: Normal casual. Waddling on prolonged walking.
neurological_exam.additional: Dysarthria after 3 minutes sustained speech. Mild dysphagia — reports difficulty with pills. NIF -58 cmH2O (borderline). No respiratory distress. No stridor.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive bilateral ptosis, diplopia, and arm fatigue worse at end of day over 3 months
patient.history_present_illness: A 34-year-old woman with no significant past medical history presented with a 3-month history of progressive bilateral ptosis, horizontal diplopia, and proximal arm weakness. She first noticed bilateral eyelid drooping approximately 3 months ago, initially only in the evenings. Over time, the ptosis became present throughout the day and progressively worsened, with the left eye more severely affected than the right. She began experiencing double vision when looking to the right, which was intermittent initially but became more frequent. She noticed that her arms became weak and fatigued when blow-drying her hair or reaching for overhead items — she could not maintain her arms elevated for more than 60 seconds. She began having difficulty chewing tough meats by the end of a meal, requiring rest breaks. Her speech became slurred and nasal after prolonged conversation, particularly noticeable in the evenings during dinner. She works as a nurse and noticed she had increasing difficulty performing overhead tasks and her handwriting was becoming affected. She denies any sensory symptoms, no headache, no visual acuity changes, no neck pain, no back pain, no bladder or bowel dysfunction. Her symptoms consistently worsen throughout the day and are significantly better in the morning after sleep. She had a brief visit to urgent care 6 weeks ago where she was told the ptosis was 'stress-related' and given a recommendation to reduce work hours. She has had no recent viral illnesses, no vaccinations, and no new medications. She is otherwise completely healthy. Her mother and aunts have no neuromuscular disease. The classic diurnal variation and fatigability pattern are well-documented on this admission.

specialized_test.test_type: Repetitive Nerve Stimulation, EMG, and NCS

findings.result: 2 mg IV test dose — improvement in ptosis within 30 seconds (ptosis reduced from complete to partial); 8 mg IV — complete resolution of ptosis and diplopia for 5 minutes
findings.significance: POSITIVE tensilon test — dramatic improvement confirms MG diagnosis

findings.result: Normal motor and sensory — normal baseline CMAP amplitudes
findings.significance: No peripheral neuropathy; LEMS excluded (normal baseline CMAP)

specialized_test.impression: Clearly abnormal RNS (16-22% decremental responses) consistent with myasthenia gravis. Positive tensilon (edrophonium) test with dramatic resolution of ptosis and diplopia confirms the diagnosis. Classic MG on electrophysiology. Single-fiber EMG would show increased jitter but is not required given this clear presentation.
recommended_actions: Anti-AChR antibody testing to confirm serostatus

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: Anti-AChR Binding 12.4 nmol/L (H), Anti-AChR Blocking 72% % (H), Anti-AChR Modulating 88% % (H).
abnormal_values_summary: Anti-AChR binding 12.4 nmol/L (markedly elevated — clearly diagnostic)

findings.density: Heterogeneous soft tissue density with areas of low attenuation
findings.description: Large anterior mediastinal mass. Lobulated borders. Displaces adjacent mediastinal structures but no clear invasion. Contains areas of necrosis or cystic degeneration.

ct.impression: Large anterior mediastinal mass 4.2 x 3.8 cm with heterogeneous enhancement. In the setting of markedly positive AChR antibodies and generalized MG, this is highly consistent with thymoma. Size and heterogeneity suggest WHO Type B2-B3 thymoma. Surgical evaluation urgent. Pre-operative MG optimization required.
recommended_actions: Urgent thoracic surgery consultation for thymectomy
Pre-operative IVIG or plasmapheresis for MG optimization
MRI chest for pre-surgical planning if needed

findings.significance: Severely increased jitter — most abnormal possible range
Very high blocking — severe NMJ failure

output.impression: Severely abnormal SFEMG — highest level of jitter and blocking. Confirms severe NMJ dysfunction consistent with markedly positive AChR antibodies and large thymoma. Not required for diagnosis (diagnosis already established) but confirms severity.

output.proposed: IVIG 2g/kg over 5 days pre-operatively for thymectomy preparation in markedly positive AChR-MG
interactions: IVIG + oral contraceptive: IVIG does not significantly affect OCP efficacy
IVIG + anti-AChR antibodies: IVIG provides immunomodulation reducing AChR antibody titers over 2-4 weeks
contraindications: Check IgA levels before IVIG — IgA deficiency can cause anaphylaxis with IVIG
Renal function check before IVIG (high-volume fluid load)
warnings: IVIG for pre-operative optimization — onset 2-5 days; peak effect 2-4 weeks
Pre-medicate with diphenhydramine and acetaminophen to prevent infusion reactions
output.formulary_status: IVIG: formulary (requires prior authorization; hospitalization indication justifies)
alternatives: Plasmapheresis (plasma exchange) 5 sessions over 10 days — faster onset than IVIG; useful when thymectomy cannot wait 2-4 weeks

signal_characteristics.DWI: No restricted diffusion suggesting necrosis not solid tumor

findings.mass_effect: Mild displacement of mediastinal structures — no invasion
findings.borders: Lobulated but circumscribed; fat plane preserved from great vessels

output.impression: MRI chest: 4.2 x 3.8 cm anterior mediastinal mass — circumscribed, no vascular invasion. WHO Type B2-B3 thymoma likely. Masaoka stage I-II (no capsular invasion apparent). Resectable. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.proposed: Pyridostigmine 60mg q4-6h AND prednisone 20mg daily for MG in woman on oral contraceptive pill
interactions: Prednisone + OCP: corticosteroids may modestly increase OCP efficacy; no dose adjustment needed
contraindications: OCP may increase corticosteroid levels via CYP3A4 — monitor for steroid side effects
Consider barrier contraception backup during immunosuppression initiation
warnings: If azathioprine added: azathioprine and OCP have no direct interaction but monitor CBC
Azathioprine: teratogenic — ensure effective contraception maintained; important in woman of reproductive age
alternatives: Mycophenolate: TERATOGENIC — avoid in women of reproductive age who may consider pregnancy

findings.significance: No pathological facilitation — LEMS excluded definitively
Normal baseline amplitude — confirms MG not LEMS

output.impression: No pathological facilitation at 50 Hz. Normal baseline CMAP. LEMS definitively excluded. Diagnosis is AChR-positive myasthenia gravis.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Myasthenia gravis, generalized (MGFA Class IIb-III), AChR antibody-positive with large thymoma (4.2 cm anterior mediastinal mass)

differential.key_features: TSH normal; anti-TPO normal; no proptosis; fatigable pattern not consistent with restrictive orbitopathy
Normal baseline CMAP; no 50Hz increment; ocular symptoms prominent (atypical LEMS); AChR markedly positive
CPEO typically symmetric, slowly progressive; AChR markedly elevated; positive tensilon test not seen in CPEO

optimal_actions.expected_finding: AChR binding 12.4 nmol/L — markedly elevated, diagnostic

optimal_actions.action: CT chest with contrast for thymoma
optimal_actions.expected_finding: 4.2 x 3.8 cm anterior mediastinal mass — thymoma

optimal_actions.action: Respiratory monitoring: NIF and FVC serially

optimal_actions.expected_finding: IVIG safe; check IgA levels; reduce AChR antibody titers before surgery

optimal_actions.action: Thoracic surgery consultation for urgent thymectomy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Resectable thymoma — thymectomy planned after MG optimization

critical_actions: Large thymoma (4.2 cm) requires urgent surgical resection after MG optimization
Pre-operative IVIG or plasmapheresis before thymectomy (markedly abnormal AChR antibodies)
Serial respiratory monitoring with NIF and FVC — borderline NIF with bulbar symptoms
Anti-AChR antibodies markedly elevated — seropositive MG diagnosis is unambiguous
Avoid teratogenic medications (mycophenolate) in woman of reproductive age
contraindicated_actions: Do NOT proceed directly to thymectomy without MG optimization (IVIG or plasmapheresis) — post-operative crisis risk
Do NOT use mycophenolate in woman of reproductive age
Do NOT use fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides for perioperative infections — worsen MG
key_reasoning_points: Classic MG presentation: young woman with fatigable ptosis, fatigable diplopia, fatigable proximal arm weakness with diurnal variation (worse evenings)
Markedly elevated AChR binding (12.4 nmol/L) with positive tensilon test — textbook straightforward MG diagnosis
Large thymoma (4.2 cm) identified on CT chest — requires surgical resection (both oncological and potential MG benefit)
Pre-operative MG optimization with IVIG or plasmapheresis is mandatory before major thoracic surgery
Mycophenolate is teratogenic and contraindicated in women of reproductive age — azathioprine with adequate contraception is preferred steroid-sparing option
